sentences.text: The genus is known from a single specimen, IVPP V.11333, consisting of a partial skull and postcranial skeleton.
The name Gongpoquansaurus was not formally published until 2014, leaving it a nomen nudum for several years prior.
The genus name refers to the Gongpoquan Basin, where the holotype locality is now part of the 2288 km² Subei Gongpoquan Dinosaur Geopark established in 2006.
The holotype specimen was collected in 1992 from the Albian Zhonggou Formation in Mazongshan, Gansu Province, China.
Lü Junchang first described the species in 1997 under the name Probactrosaurus mazongshanensis.
The genus Gongpoquansaurus was formally erected in 2014 after studies showed it was less derived than Probactrosaurus.
Phylogenetic analysis indicates Gongpoquansaurus is more basal and further from Hadrosauridae than Probactrosaurus.
Gongpoquansaurus forms a clade of Eurasian hadrosauroids including Koshisaurus, Batyrosaurus, Ratchasimasaurus, and Proa valdearinnoensis.
Gongpoquansaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately between 129 and 114 million years ago in the Barremian and Aptian stages.
Fossil evidence places Gongpoquansaurus in the Albian stage, between 113.2 and 110.1 million years ago.
